mara.activity: Wake, wash my face, brush my teeth, dress in work clothes, and check quietly whether Julian needs anything without disturbing him for long.
mara.intention: Start the day and make a discreet welfare check.

mara.activity: Make coffee and a quiet breakfast, carrying the mug and food to the dining table. I leave tea bags and the brass spoon on the kitchen sink-cabinet countertop for later.
mara.intention: Eat before work while keeping the morning calm.

mara.activity: Prepare ginger tea and carry it with painkillers and a fresh water bottle to Julian, checking his temperature and settling the items within reach.
mara.intention: Take over a small practical decision and support Julian without making him talk.

mara.activity: Return to the second bedroom, open the laptop, take the active manuscript from the canvas folder, and arrange the proof pages and printed style sheet on the desk.
mara.intention: Set up the regular Friday editing block.

mara.activity: Edit the manuscript against the printed style sheet, recording precise notes and saving the file as I go.
mara.intention: Make steady progress on the active manuscript.

mara.activity: Stand, stretch, and check whether Julian needs more tea, water, or medication. I refill the mug or bottle if needed and return to the desk.
mara.intention: Pause without losing the work rhythm while staying attentive.

mara.activity: Continue editing, reread difficult passages aloud under my breath, and save the revised manuscript before closing the morning work block.
mara.intention: Finish the scheduled manuscript work carefully.

mara.activity: Make a light lunch in the kitchen, carry it to the dining table, and eat while listening to the radio. I rinse the dishes and leave the kitchen reasonably clear.
mara.intention: Take a proper break and prepare food simply while Julian rests.

mara.activity: Return to the desk and finish the weekly invoices, checking amounts and drafting any brief follow-up messages for unpaid accounts.
mara.intention: Complete the Friday administrative work before it becomes urgent.

mara.activity: Take a short break and check on Julian, bringing fresh ginger tea or water if needed and checking his temperature quietly.
mara.intention: Keep the care routine unobtrusive but consistent.

mara.activity: Back up the week's files, clear the desk, return the proof pages to the canvas folder, and write a concise list for Monday.
mara.intention: Finish the working week with the files and physical workspace under control.

mara.activity: Make an easy early dinner for both of us: toast with melted cheddar and sliced vegetables. I carry Julian's portion and water to him, then leave my plate covered in the kitchen for later.
mara.intention: Prepare food that requires little effort and can be eaten whenever Julian feels able.

mara.activity: Wash my hands, change into walking clothes, put on walking shoes, and check once more that Julian has water and can call me if needed.
mara.intention: Prepare for the usual decompression walk without leaving him unsupported.

mara.activity: Walk around the neighborhood at a brisk but comfortable pace, letting the day's watchfulness settle.
mara.intention: Decompress and clear my head before the evening.

mara.activity: Return home, wash my hands, reheat my dinner, and eat at the dining table. I check on Julian briefly and bring him anything practical he requests.
mara.intention: Eat before the quiet evening and remain available without hovering.

mara.activity: Read or watch a quiet program with Julian in the living room, keeping the volume low and checking discreetly whether he needs water, painkillers, or another blanket. When I finish reading, I leave the book face-down with its receipt marking the page on the small shelving unit by the sofa.
mara.intention: Share a calm evening while accommodating his limited energy.

mara.activity: Wash the dishes, check Julian's temperature, put painkillers and water within reach, and make sure he is settled for the night.
mara.intention: Close the day with the usual practical care.

mara.activity: Wash my face, brush my teeth, change into sleep clothes, and put my reading glasses on the nightstand by my bed.
mara.intention: Wind down and keep my things in their usual places.

mara.activity: Put my phone on charge by the wardrobe, read a few pages in bed, then turn out the light and go to sleep.
mara.intention: Keep the phone out of reach overnight and get enough rest.

julian.activity: Wake slowly, take my temperature, drink water, and sit on the edge of the bed before getting up.
julian.intention: Check how unwell I am without rushing into the day.

julian.activity: Wash, brush my teeth, and change into comfortable clothes, leaving my sleep clothes in the hamper.
julian.intention: Do the minimum morning routine without exhausting myself.

julian.activity: Make weak tea and carry a small breakfast of crackers and a little banana to the living-room sofa, then eat slowly.
julian.intention: Get some fluid and food down before resting.

julian.activity: Rest or sleep on the large sofa with my phone nearby, keeping museum notifications silenced except for anything genuinely urgent.
julian.intention: Recover rather than trying to work through the illness.

julian.activity: Check my temperature, take an ordinary dose of medicine after checking the label, and refill my water.
julian.intention: Manage the symptoms and notice whether anything has changed.

julian.activity: Send one brief museum message confirming that I remain ill and will be unavailable today, then put the phone back on silent.
julian.intention: Reduce work guilt by communicating clearly without opening a full work session.

julian.activity: Eat a small lunch at the kitchen island if I can manage it, using whatever light food is available, and leave the dishes by the sink afterward.
julian.intention: Eat something small without cooking a proper meal.

julian.activity: Return to the large sofa for quiet rest, dozing or listening to low music and asking Mara for help only if I genuinely need it.
julian.intention: Keep conversation and stimulation low while my energy is poor.

julian.activity: Take a lukewarm shower, brush my teeth, and put on fresh comfortable clothes.
julian.intention: Freshen up without attempting a demanding routine.

julian.activity: Rest in the second bedroom with the phone on silent, making only a short note of any museum matter that can wait.
julian.intention: Give myself a quieter room and stop work from expanding.

julian.activity: Order a simple dinner and drinks by phone rather than cooking, then clear a small space at the dining table.
julian.intention: Arrange an easy evening meal while I still have enough energy to do it.

julian.activity: Collect the delivered food, carry it to the dining table, and eat a small portion slowly.
julian.intention: Have dinner without standing in the kitchen or overexerting myself.

julian.activity: Put the remaining food into a container and leave the used plate and fork by the sink, then return to the sofa.
julian.intention: Prevent food waste while postponing nonessential washing up.

julian.activity: Watch something quiet or listen to low music from the large sofa, keeping conversation minimal while sharing the room if Mara is there.
julian.intention: Have a calm evening without pretending to be well enough for the usual Friday social routine.

julian.activity: Check my temperature once more, wash my face, brush my teeth, and refill the water bottle.
julian.intention: Finish the day clean and prepared for another poor night of sleep.

julian.activity: Get into bed, silence work notifications completely, and leave the phone and water within reach on the nightstand.
julian.intention: Set a firm boundary around rest and avoid answering late museum messages.

julian.activity: Rest quietly and try to sleep, using tissues or water if needed.
julian.intention: Allow the body to recover rather than measuring the night by productivity.
